title: Equality Case of Chebyshev's Sum Inequality via the Discrete Covariance Identity
description: Mathlib proves Chebyshev's sum inequality (#s · ∑ fᵢgᵢ ≥ (∑ fᵢ)(∑ gᵢ) for monovarying f, g) but records no equality case and no underlying algebraic identity. We supply the discrete covariance identity ∑ᵢ∑ⱼ (fᵢ−fⱼ)(gᵢ−gⱼ) = 2(#s · ∑ fᵢgᵢ − (∑ fᵢ)(∑ gᵢ)) — valid with no order hypotheses — re-derive Chebyshev from it, and characterise equality exactly: for monovarying f, g equality holds iff every pair i, j satisfies fᵢ = fⱼ or gᵢ = gⱼ; for monotone sequences this collapses to the textbook statement that f or g is constant on s.

originalContributions: covariance_identity: the order-free discrete covariance identity ∑ᵢ∑ⱼ (fᵢ−fⱼ)(gᵢ−gⱼ) = 2(#s·∑ fᵢgᵢ − (∑ fᵢ)(∑ gᵢ)), the finite analogue of 2n²·Cov(f,g) — not present in Mathlib
term_nonneg: each summand (fᵢ−fⱼ)(gᵢ−gⱼ) is nonnegative under MonovaryOn
chebyshev_sum: Chebyshev's sum inequality re-derived as a one-line corollary of the identity (Mathlib proves the same bound by a different route)
chebyshev_sum_eq_iff: the exact equality characterisation — for monovarying f, g, equality holds iff ∀ i j ∈ s, fᵢ = fⱼ ∨ gᵢ = gⱼ — absent from Mathlib
chebyshev_sum_eq_iff_const: the textbook monotone form — equality iff f is constant on s or g is constant on s — via the extreme-pair (min'/max') argument

overview.historicalContext: Pafnuty Chebyshev's sum inequality (1880s) states that for two real sequences sorted in the same order, the average of the products dominates the product of the averages: (1/n)∑ aᵢbᵢ ≥ ((1/n)∑ aᵢ)((1/n)∑ bᵢ). It is the discrete shadow of the fact that two comonotone random variables have nonnegative covariance, and it descends from the rearrangement inequality by summing the rearrangement bound over the n cyclic shifts of one sequence. Mathlib formalises the inequality itself (MonovaryOn.sum_mul_sum_le_card_mul_sum) but stops short of its equality case. The classical answer — equality exactly when one of the sequences is constant — is the natural rigidity companion, and like the equality cases of the AM–GM, Bernoulli, and triangle inequalities it is what pins down extremisers.
overview.problemStatement:
Let $s$ be a finite index set, $n = \#s$, and $f, g : s \to \mathbb{R}$ monovary (sort in the same order). Chebyshev's sum inequality reads

$$\Big(\sum_{i} f_i\Big)\Big(\sum_{i} g_i\Big) \;\le\; n \sum_{i} f_i g_i.$$

Characterise the equality case. Concretely, prove the algebraic identity driving the inequality and show that

$$n \sum_i f_i g_i = \Big(\sum_i f_i\Big)\Big(\sum_i g_i\Big) \iff \forall\, i, j,\ f_i = f_j \ \text{or}\ g_i = g_j,$$

which for monotone $f, g$ means $f$ is constant or $g$ is constant on $s$.
overview.proofStrategy:
Everything is generated by one identity.

1. covariance_identity expands the symmetric double sum: ∑ᵢ∑ⱼ (fᵢ−fⱼ)(gᵢ−gⱼ) = 2(n·∑ fᵢgᵢ − (∑ fᵢ)(∑ gᵢ)). The proof distributes the product, splits the four double sums (two collapse to n·∑ fg via sum over a constant index, two to (∑ f)(∑ g) via Finset.mul_sum / sum_mul), and closes with ring. No ordering is used.

2. term_nonneg: under MonovaryOn, a trichotomy on gᵢ vs gⱼ shows (fᵢ−fⱼ) and (gᵢ−gⱼ) have the same sign, so each summand is ≥ 0 (nlinarith with the relevant product).

3. chebyshev_sum: the double sum is a sum of nonnegative terms, hence ≥ 0; substituting the identity gives the inequality immediately.

4. chebyshev_sum_eq_iff: equality means the covariance double sum is 0; since every term is ≥ 0, Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg (applied to the outer then inner sum) forces every (fᵢ−fⱼ)(gᵢ−gⱼ) = 0, and mul_eq_zero gives fᵢ = fⱼ ∨ gᵢ = gⱼ. The converse is unconditional: if every term vanishes the double sum is 0, so the identity yields equality.

5. chebyshev_sum_eq_iff_const: for monotone f, g (hence monovarying), the extreme-pair argument shows a non-constant monotone function already differs between min' s and max' s; so if both f and g varied, the (min', max') pair would violate the pairwise condition. Contrapositive plus the previous theorem gives the constant-or-constant dichotomy.
keyInsights: The single identity ∑ᵢ∑ⱼ (fᵢ−fⱼ)(gᵢ−gⱼ) = 2(n·∑ fg − (∑ f)(∑ g)) simultaneously proves the inequality (RHS of terms ≥ 0) and its equality case (terms = 0), with no order hypothesis needed for the identity itself.
It is the unnormalised finite analogue of 2n²·Cov(f, g); Chebyshev's inequality is exactly 'covariance of comonotone sequences is nonnegative'.
The clean pairwise equality condition ∀ i j, fᵢ = fⱼ ∨ gᵢ = gⱼ is stronger and more informative than 'f or g constant', which is equivalent to it only under monotonicity.
Monotonicity makes the (min', max') pair extremal: a non-constant monotone sequence must differ at the endpoints, which is precisely what forces the dichotomy in the textbook statement.
This complements Mathlib's rearrangement equality cases (which characterise equality of the permuted scalar product), giving the Chebyshev/card-form equality that Mathlib's Chebyshev file omits.
prerequisites: Finite sums over Finset and the double-sum manipulations (Finset.mul_sum, sum_mul, sum_eq_zero)

conclusion.summary: We isolated the discrete covariance identity underlying Chebyshev's sum inequality, re-derived the inequality from it, and characterised its equality case both exactly (pairwise fᵢ = fⱼ ∨ gᵢ = gⱼ) and in the textbook monotone form (f or g constant on s). All five results are fully machine-checked and depend only on the foundational axioms (0 sorries, 0 axioms).
conclusion.implications: The identity is reusable infrastructure: it gives the Cauchy–Schwarz/variance bound (f = g case), the equality analysis for sorted-sequence inequalities, and a template for the covariance viewpoint on monotone correlation. The equality case completes Mathlib's Chebyshev file, mirroring the rigidity companions already in the gallery for AM–GM, Bernoulli, and the triangle inequality.
openQuestions: State and prove the strict version with an explicit lower bound: n·∑ fg − (∑ f)(∑ g) ≥ (1/2)·max-pair-defect, quantifying how far from equality non-constant monovarying sequences sit.
Derive the weighted Chebyshev sum inequality and its equality case from a weighted covariance identity ∑ᵢ∑ⱼ wᵢwⱼ(fᵢ−fⱼ)(gᵢ−gⱼ).
Characterise equality of the rearrangement inequality itself (∑ fᵢ g_{σ(i)} = ∑ fᵢ gᵢ) for non-injective comparisons, the TODO flagged in Mathlib's Rearrangement file.
